messages:
Sam (sales): Heads up — BetaMed POC hitting intermittent JSON parse failures when they enable streaming + function_call. UX shows "Unexpected end of input" mid-response. Non-streaming works.
Sam (sales): Timeline: they spin up 8 parallel streams from their frontend. Failures started after a ramp test.
deploy-bot: rate_limit alert for acct-betamed at 1942101512 - burst=412 limit=400 - returning 429s.
Sam (sales): Small log snip from their capture:
```
stream_chunk: {"choices": [{"delta": {"tool_call": "{\"name\":\"extract\",\"arguments\":{\"patient_summary\":\"Started...\"}\"}"}}]
stream_chunk: {"choices": [{"delta": {"tool_call": "...partial json\"}}], "finish_reason": "stop"}
client: JSON.parse error: Unexpected end of JSON input
```
Priya (eng): Likely two contributing bits: (A) 429s sever streams mid-output leaving unterminated JSON; (B) our incremental emitter can split the tool_call JSON across deltas without a clear boundary token, so client may try to parse mid-assemble.
Leo (solutions): Quick mitigations for POC so BetaMed can continue demoing: 1) ask them to cap frontend concurrency to 4 streams max; 2) add a stream-end sentinel or sequence numbers (e.g. emit "__END_OBJECT__" after the tool_call payload) so their parser can detect completeness; 3) client fallback: on parse fail, re-request same payload with stream=false.
Sam (sales): They asked if adding a sentinel is safe for security/compliance — this goes into their security questionnaire.
sec-bot: Note: any sentinel inserted in content may require PII review. Avoid embedding PHI in logs; prefer structural signaling (seq id + final=true) rather than user-visible magic tokens.
Tom (infra): I can temporarily raise their burst cap to 800 for 48h to get through the POC. Also enabling tenant-level verbose streaming traces.
Fin-Alex: For pricing — temporary cap bump is covered under our POC support policy (no extra charge for first 72h). If they go long-term, we'll include recommended committed capacity in the quote.
Priya (eng): For short-term server-side hardening: we'll add a tolerant assembler that keeps partial tool_call fragments and only emits a completed JSON object when the final chunk is received or finish_reason != null. ETA: patch branch tomorrow, target release in next patch window. Creating INF-3502.
QA-Mina: Filed INF-3502: "streamed tool_call boundary robustness (beta)" and assigned to Priya. Steps: reproduce with parallel streams >6, simulate 429 mid-stream, validate client fallback behavior.
Sam (sales): I've passed mitigation steps + fallback snippet to BetaMed and asked them to lower frontend concurrency. Also sent them our security note about avoiding PII in sentinels.
BetaMed-ops (via Sam): Confirmed: after lowering concurrency -> streams succeed. They saw one parse failure that was resolved by retry (non-stream).
Sam (sales): Keeping thread open until INF-3502 closes. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
